checks.label: In the first time interval τ = RC the voltage falls to 0.368 of its initial value, since e^(−1) = 0.368: at 1τ the model keeps 0.368 of the start and a 10 V start reads 3.68 V, at every R and C tried

RC is the time during which the charge drops to 1/e of the initial value, and has dimensions of time: 100 kΩ × 470 µF gives 47 s, 10 kΩ × 1000 µF gives 10 s, and one RC leaves 1/e of the gap on every curve drawn

An object cools at a rate proportional to the difference between its temperature and the ambient temperature: on every cooling curve, the rate of fall measured at many times divided by the gap to the room is the same everywhere

The rate of growth is proportional to the current function value, here run downhill: on every capacitor curve, discharging and charging, the slope measured at many times divided by the gap still to close is the same everywhere
Every gap bar keeps 0.368 of the bar one time constant before it, in every mode, at every handle setting and with R and C across their ranges, and every pill reads × 0.368
Charging is the discharge flipped and lifted: at every time the charging and discharging voltages add to the 10 V supply, so the charging gap bars match the discharge bars
By the rule the gap never closes: at 5τ the charge is 99.3% with 0.07 V to go, 400 V leaves 2.7 V, and every curve drawn stays strictly between its start and its line
The model returns the time constant, the share of the gap left and the reading the picture shows, at every handle setting and switch setting on every demonstration screen
The 30 s point sits on the curve between the marks: e^(−30/47) ≈ 0.528 gives 5.28 V, and with a bigger R the same 30 s is fewer time constants, so it sits higher

Every number follows its rule: 3.68, 1.35 and 0.50 V (slips 0 V and 1.84 V); 47 s, 94 s and 141 s; 243 V (slips 659 V and 0 V); 0.632, 6.32, 8.65 and 9.50 V; 63.2, 86.5, 95.0, 98.2 and 99.3% (slips 12.64 V, 126.4% and 3.99 V); 2.7 V (slip 80 V); 70, 25.8, 45.8, 29.5 and 23.5 °C (slips 33.1 and 64.2 °C); 2.13, 0.119, 0.60 and 4.40 V (slip 6.72 V); 10 s (slips 10,000 s and 0.01 s); 6.8 and 36.8 °C (slips 10.8 and 48.4 °C); and each answer offered is the value its own working gives
Before an answer, nothing in a puzzle's picture gives it away, and a right answer shows it
Each puzzle offers three answers and takes only its right one, and every wrong answer has a hint of its own
Every demonstration has finished arriving within its time (at most 4.5 s), none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s
